ei.title: Practice 01 — 도서관 도서 검열에 대한 반대 입장 표명
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본2

fullPassage: Dear Mr. Dennison: Thanks for thinking of me as a sponsor of your boycott. Like you, I want our children to grow up in a moral society. But I am afraid I can't give you permission to use my name as a support for Parents for Library Censorship. The fact is, you and I are on different sides of this issue ― namely, I am for freedom of speech and against censorship in any form. While I agree with you that some of the books on the list are of questionable quality and taste, I also feel just as strongly that no one person or organization has the right to determine what is 'suitable' literature for other people. I spoke out very strongly against library censorship at a recent parent-teachers meeting and I will do likewise when I have the opportunity. Sincerely, John Thomson

questions.passage: Dear Mr. Dennison: Thanks for thinking of me as a sponsor of your boycott. Like you, I want our children to grow up in a (A)[moral / immoral] society. But I am afraid I can't give you permission to use my name as a support for Parents for Library Censorship. The fact is, you and I are on different sides of this issue ― namely, I am for (B)[freedom / restriction] of speech and against censorship in any form. While I agree with you that some of the books on the list are of questionable quality and taste, I also feel just as strongly that no one person or organization has the right to (C)[determine / ignore] what is 'suitable' literature for other people. I spoke out very strongly against library censorship at a recent parent-teachers meeting and I will do likewise when I have the opportunity. Sincerely, John Thomson
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① moral — freedom — determine: 원문 일치. 도덕적 사회(moral), 언론의 자유(freedom), 결정할 권리(determine)에 부합
❌ ② immoral — freedom — determine: (A) immoral(비도덕적인)은 moral의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ moral — restriction — determine: (B) restriction(제한)은 freedom(자유)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ④ moral — freedom — ignore: (C) ignore(무시하다)는 determine(결정하다)과 의미상 대립하여 부적절
det.tip: moral society(도덕적 사회) + freedom of speech(언론의 자유) + right to determine(결정할 권리)

questions.passage: Dear Mr. Dennison: Thanks for thinking of me as a sponsor of your boycott. Like you, I want our children to grow up in a moral society. But I am afraid I can't give you (A)[permission / refusal] to use my name as a support for Parents for Library Censorship. The fact is, you and I are on different sides of this issue ― namely, I am for freedom of speech and against censorship in any form. While I agree with you that some of the books on the list are of (B)[questionable / excellent] quality and taste, I also feel just as strongly that no one person or organization has the right to determine what is '(C)[suitable / unsuitable]' literature for other people. I spoke out very strongly against library censorship at a recent parent-teachers meeting and I will do likewise when I have the opportunity. Sincerely, John Thomson
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① refusal — questionable — suitable: (A) refusal(거절)은 permission(허락)의 반의어로 문맥 왜곡
✅ ② permission — questionable — suitable: 원문 일치. 이름 사용 허락(permission), 품질이 의심스러운(questionable), 적합한 문학(suitable)에 부합
❌ ③ permission — excellent — suitable: (B) excellent(우수한)는 questionable(의심스러운)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ④ permission — questionable — unsuitable: (C) unsuitable(부적합한)은 suitable의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: give permission(허락하다) + questionable quality(의심스러운 품질) + 'suitable' literature(적합한 문학)

questions.passage: Dear Mr. Dennison: Thanks for thinking of me as a (A)[sponsor / opponent] of your boycott. Like you, I want our children to grow up in a moral society. But I am afraid I can't give you permission to use my name as a support for Parents for Library Censorship. The fact is, you and I are on different sides of this issue ― namely, I am for freedom of speech and (B)[against / for] censorship in any form. While I agree with you that some of the books on the list are of questionable quality and taste, I also feel just as strongly that no one person or organization has the right to determine what is 'suitable' literature for other people. I spoke out very strongly against library censorship at a recent parent-teachers meeting and I will do likewise when I have the (C)[opportunity / obstacle]. Sincerely, John Thomson
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① sponsor — against — obstacle: (C) obstacle(장애물)은 opportunity(기회)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② sponsor — for — opportunity: (B) for(찬성하는)는 against(반대하는)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ opponent — against — opportunity: (A) opponent(반대자)는 sponsor(후원자)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ④ sponsor — against — opportunity: 원문 일치. 후원자(sponsor), 검열에 반대(against), 기회가 있을 때(opportunity)에 부합
det.tip: sponsor of your boycott(불매운동 후원자) + against censorship(검열에 반대) + have the opportunity(기회가 있을 때)

questions.passage: Dear Mr. Dennison: Thanks for thinking of me as a sponsor of your boycott. Like you, I want our children to grow up in a ①<u>corrupt</u> society. But I am afraid I can't give you ②<u>permission</u> to use my name as a support for Parents for Library Censorship. The fact is, you and I are on different sides of this issue ― namely, I am for freedom of speech and ③<u>against</u> censorship in any form. While I agree with you that some of the books on the list are of questionable quality and taste, I also feel just as strongly that no one person or organization has the right to determine what is 'suitable' literature for other people. I spoke out very strongly against library censorship at a recent parent-teachers meeting and I will do likewise when I have the ④<u>opportunity</u>. Sincerely, John Thomson
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 도덕적 사회를 원한다고 했으므로 'moral'이 맞음. immoral(비도덕적인)은 부적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① corrupt — 원문은 moral(도덕적인). 아이들이 도덕적 사회에서 자라기를 원한다고 했으므로 corrupt(부패한)는 정반대 의미
❌ ② permission — 원문 일치. 이름 사용 허락을 줄 수 없다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ against — 원문 일치. 검열에 반대한다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ opportunity — 원문 일치. 기회가 있을 때마다 반대 의사를 밝히겠다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: want our children to grow up in a moral society = 도덕적인 사회에서 자라기를 원함. corrupt(부패한)로 바꾸면 글의 의도와 완전히 반대

questions.passage: Dear Mr. Dennison: Thanks for thinking of me as a sponsor of your boycott. Like you, I want our children to grow up in a moral society. But I am afraid I can't give you permission to use my name as a ②<u>opposition</u> for Parents for Library Censorship. The fact is, you and I are on ③<u>different</u> sides of this issue ― namely, I am for freedom of speech and against censorship in any form. While I agree with you that some of the books on the list are of questionable quality and taste, I also feel just as ④<u>strongly</u> that no one person or organization has the ①<u>right</u> to determine what is 'suitable' literature for other people. I spoke out very strongly against library censorship at a recent parent-teachers meeting and I will do likewise when I have the opportunity. Sincerely, John Thomson
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 도서 검열 부모 단체에 대한 '지지'가 문맥에 맞음. opposition(반대)는 부적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① opposition — 원문은 support(지지). John Thomson에게 이름을 '지지'로 사용하게 해달라는 내용인데, opposition(반대)로 바꾸면 요청의 의도와 완전히 상충
❌ ② different — 원문 일치. 두 사람이 서로 다른 입장이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ strongly — 원문 일치. 강하게 반대 의사를 표명한다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ right — 원문 일치. 결정할 권리가 없다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: use my name as a support for Parents for Library Censorship = 도서 검열 단체에 대한 지지로 내 이름을 사용. opposition(반대)로 바꾸면 반대 의미

questions.passage: Dear Mr. Dennison: Thanks for thinking of me as a sponsor of your ①<u>boycott</u>. Like you, I want our children to grow up in a moral society. But I am afraid I can't give you permission to use my name as a support for Parents for Library Censorship. The fact is, you and I are on different sides of this issue ― namely, I am for ②<u>freedom</u> of speech and against censorship in any form. While I agree with you that some of the books on the list are of ③<u>questionable</u> quality and taste, I also feel just as strongly that no one person or organization has the right to ④<u>protect</u> what is 'suitable' literature for other people. I spoke out very strongly against library censorship at a recent parent-teachers meeting and I will do likewise when I have the opportunity. Sincerely, John Thomson
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 개인이나 단체가 '결정할' 권리가 없다가 문맥에 맞음. protect(보호하다)는 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① boycott — 원문 일치. 불매운동의 후원자로 생각해 줘서 감사하다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② freedom — 원문 일치. 언론의 자유를 지지한다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ questionable — 원문 일치. 목록의 일부 도서가 품질이 의심스럽다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ④ protect — 원문은 determine(결정하다). 누가 '결정할' 권리도 없다는 것이 핵심 주장인데, protect(보호하다)로 바꾸면 전혀 다른 의미가 됨
det.tip: right to determine = 결정할 권리. 적합한 문학이 무엇인지 결정할 권리가 없다는 주장이 글의 핵심

questions.passage: Dear Mr. Dennison: Thanks for thinking of me as a sponsor of your boycott. Like you, I want our children to grow up in a __________ society. But I am afraid I can't give you permission to use my name as a support for Parents for Library Censorship. The fact is, you and I are on different sides of this issue ― namely, I am for freedom of speech and against censorship in any form. While I agree with you that some of the books on the list are of questionable quality and taste, I also feel just as strongly that no one person or organization has the right to determine what is 'suitable' literature for other people. I spoke out very strongly against library censorship at a recent parent-teachers meeting and I will do likewise when I have the opportunity. Sincerely, John Thomson
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① moral — 도덕적인. 아이들이 도덕적 사회에서 자라기를 원한다는 문맥에 정확히 부합
❌ ② questionable — 의심스러운. 사회를 묘사할 때 도덕성 기준이 아닌 품질 의심의 의미이므로 부적절
❌ ③ suitable — 적합한. '적합한 사회'는 이 편지에서 강조하는 도덕적 가치와 다른 의미
❌ ④ afraid — 두려워하는. 사회를 묘사하는 형용사로 부적절
det.tip: grow up in a moral society = 도덕적인 사회에서 자라다 — 두 사람이 공통적으로 원하는 바

questions.passage: Dear Mr. Dennison: Thanks for thinking of me as a sponsor of your boycott. Like you, I want our children to grow up in a moral society. But I am afraid I can't give you permission to use my name as a support for Parents for Library __________. The fact is, you and I are on different sides of this issue ― namely, I am for freedom of speech and against censorship in any form. While I agree with you that some of the books on the list are of questionable quality and taste, I also feel just as strongly that no one person or organization has the right to determine what is 'suitable' literature for other people. I spoke out very strongly against library censorship at a recent parent-teachers meeting and I will do likewise when I have the opportunity. Sincerely, John Thomson
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① freedom — 자유. library freedom(도서관 자유)이라는 표현은 본문 맥락과 어울리지 않음
✅ ② censorship — 검열. library censorship(도서관 검열)에 강하게 반대했다는 원문 문맥에 정확히 부합
❌ ③ speech — 말/연설. library speech(도서관 연설)는 문맥에 맞지 않음
❌ ④ permission — 허락. library permission은 문맥에서 사용된 표현이 아님
det.tip: spoke out against library censorship = 도서관 검열에 맞서 강하게 발언했다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다른 사람에게 적합한 문학이 무엇인지 '결정할' 권리가 없다 → determine
det.analysis:
✅ ① determine — 결정하다. 어느 누구도 다른 사람에게 맞는 문학이 무엇인지 결정할 권리가 없다는 핵심 주장
❌ ② support — 지지하다. 적합한 문학을 지지할 권리가 없다는 것은 글의 맥락과 맞지 않음
❌ ③ ignore — 무시하다. 권리를 무시한다는 것은 문맥과 다른 의미
❌ ④ avoid — 피하다. 문학을 피할 권리가 없다는 것은 문맥 왜곡
det.tip: right to determine what is 'suitable' = 무엇이 적합한지 결정할 권리 — 검열 반대의 핵심 논거

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 permission과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① denial — 거부. 반대 의미
✅ ② approval — 승인, 허락. permission(허락)과 가장 유사한 의미
❌ ③ request — 요청. 허락이 아닌 요청의 의미
❌ ④ opinion — 의견. 전혀 다른 의미
det.tip: give permission = give approval = 허락을 주다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 questionable과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① certain — 확실한. 반대 의미
✅ ② doubtful — 의심스러운. questionable(의심스러운)과 가장 유사한 의미
❌ ③ outstanding — 뛰어난. 품질이 뛰어나다는 것은 questionable과 반대
❌ ④ acceptable — 받아들일 수 있는. questionable과 반대 의미
det.tip: questionable quality and taste = 의심스러운 품질과 취향 — doubtful quality와 동일한 의미

det.tip: 'suitable' literature = 'appropriate' literature = 적합한 문학

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 strongly와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① boldly — 대담하게. strongly와 유사한 의미
❌ ② clearly — 분명하게. 강도가 아닌 명확성의 의미
❌ ③ firmly — 단호하게. strongly와 유사한 의미
✅ ④ weakly — 약하게. strongly(강하게)의 반의어
det.tip: feel just as strongly = 마찬가지로 강하게 느끼다 ↔ weakly(약하게)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 sponsor와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① benefactor — 후원자, 은인. sponsor와 유사한 의미
❌ ② advocate — 지지자, 옹호자. sponsor와 유사한 의미

❌ ④ ally — 동맹, 지지자. sponsor와 유사한 의미
det.tip: sponsor(후원자) ↔ opponent(반대자) — 지지/후원 관계 vs 반대 관계

questions.passage:
(A) John wrote in his letter: "no one person or organization has the <u>right</u> to determine what is 'suitable' literature for other people."

(B) She turned <u>right</u> at the corner and found the library.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 right의 의미가 (A)와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: (A) right = 권리 → authority(권한, 권리)와 가장 가까움
det.analysis:
❌ ① correct — 올바른. right의 형용사 의미(옳은)이나 (A)에서는 명사로 사용됨
❌ ② direction — 방향. (B)에서의 right(오른쪽)과 관련된 의미
✅ ③ authority — 권한, 권리. (A)의 right(권리)와 가장 유사한 의미
❌ ④ immediately — 즉시. 부사로서의 right 의미
det.tip: have the right to do = ~할 권리가 있다. right as a noun = 권리(authority/entitlement)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the practice of officially examining books, films, or news and suppressing unacceptable parts"

det.korean: 공식적으로 책·영화·뉴스를 검사하고 용납할 수 없는 부분을 억압하는 관행 → censorship(검열)
det.analysis:
❌ ① freedom — 자유. 정의에서 묘사되는 억압 행위와 반대 개념
❌ ② permission — 허락. 억압이 아닌 허가의 의미
❌ ③ boycott — 불매운동. 구매 거부 행위로 전혀 다른 의미
✅ ④ censorship — 검열. 공식적으로 출판물·미디어를 검사하고 금지하는 행위의 정확한 정의
det.tip: censorship = 검열 — 책, 영화, 뉴스 등의 내용을 공식적으로 심사하고 부적절한 부분을 제거하는 행위

questions.passage: I also feel just as strongly that no one person or organization has the right to __________ (determine) what is 'suitable' literature for other people.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: has the right to __________ (determine) → to 부정사 뒤이므로 동사원형 그대로 사용
det.analysis: 원형 유지: have the right to + 동사원형. 'to'는 전치사가 아닌 to부정사이므로 동사원형 사용
det.tip: have the right to determine = 결정할 권리가 있다 → to 뒤에 동사원형

questions.passage: While I agree with you that some of the books on the list are of __________ (question) quality and taste, I also feel just as strongly that no one person or organization has the right to determine what is 'suitable' literature for other people.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: question(질문/의심) → questionable(의심스러운). of __________ quality 구조에서 형용사가 필요. -able 접미사로 형용사화
det.tip: question(동사/명사) → questionable(형용사) — 의심의 여지가 있는, 불확실한

questions.passage: Dear Mr. Dennison: Thanks for thinking of me as a sponsor of your boycott. Like you, I want our children to grow up in a moral society. But I am afraid I can't give you permission to use my name as a support for Parents for Library Censorship. The fact is, you and I are on different sides of this issue ― namely, I am for __________ and against censorship in any form. While I agree with you that some of the books on the list are of questionable quality and taste, I also feel just as strongly that no one person or organization has the right to determine what is 'suitable' literature for other people. I spoke out very strongly against library censorship at a recent parent-teachers meeting and I will do likewise when I have the opportunity. Sincerely, John Thomson
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: I am for '언론의 자유'라고 자신의 입장을 밝힘 → freedom of speech
det.analysis:
❌ ① library censorship — 도서관 검열. 필자가 반대하는 대상이므로 'I am for'와 양립 불가
❌ ② moral society — 도덕적 사회. 두 사람이 공통적으로 원하지만, 이 문장의 대조적 논지와 다름
❌ ③ parental control — 부모의 통제. 본문에 등장하지 않는 표현
✅ ④ freedom of speech — 언론의 자유. 'I am for freedom of speech'가 원문으로, 필자의 핵심 입장
det.tip: I am for freedom of speech and against censorship = 언론의 자유를 지지하고 검열에 반대 — 필자 입장의 핵심

questions.passage: Dear Mr. Dennison: Thanks for thinking of me as a sponsor of your boycott. Like you, I want our children to grow up in a moral society. But I am afraid I can't give you permission to use my name as a support for Parents for Library Censorship. The fact is, you and I are __________ ― namely, I am for freedom of speech and against censorship in any form. While I agree with you that some of the books on the list are of questionable quality and taste, I also feel just as strongly that no one person or organization has the right to determine what is 'suitable' literature for other people. I spoke out very strongly against library censorship at a recent parent-teachers meeting and I will do likewise when I have the opportunity. Sincerely, John Thomson
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나와 당신은 이 문제에서 '다른 입장에 있다' → on different sides of this issue
det.analysis:
❌ ① for freedom of speech — 언론의 자유 지지. you and I are 뒤에 이것을 넣으면 두 사람이 모두 언론의 자유를 지지하는 것처럼 되지만, 실제로는 서로 다른 입장임
❌ ② against censorship in any form — 어떤 검열에도 반대. 편지에서 필자만 그런 입장이고 두 사람 모두 해당하는 서술이 아님
✅ ③ on different sides of this issue — 이 문제에서 서로 다른 입장. 원문 일치. 다음 namely 절로 입장 차이를 설명하는 흐름에 부합
❌ ④ against library censorship — 도서관 검열에 반대. 편지 발신자(필자)만의 입장이고 수신자는 반대하므로 두 사람 모두에 해당하지 않음
det.tip: you and I are on different sides of this issue = 우리는 이 문제에서 다른 입장 — 편지를 쓰는 근본 이유
